optimized_sql:
WITH filtered_cd AS (
    SELECT cd_demo_sk
    FROM customer_demographics
    WHERE cd_gender = 'F'
      AND cd_marital_status = 'W'
      AND cd_education_status = 'College'
),
filtered_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_year = 2001
),
filtered_promos AS (
    SELECT p_promo_sk
    FROM promotion
    WHERE p_channel_email = 'N' OR p_channel_event = 'N'
),
top_item_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.i_item_id
    FROM item i
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM store_sales ss
        JOIN filtered_cd cd ON ss.ss_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
        JOIN filtered_dates dt ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = dt.d_date_sk
        JOIN filtered_promos pr ON ss.ss_promo_sk = pr.p_promo_sk
        WHERE ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    )
    ORDER BY i.i_item_id
    LIMIT 100
),
top_item_keys AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_sk
    FROM item i
    JOIN top_item_ids t ON i.i_item_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM t.i_item_id
),
fact_agg AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_item_sk,
           SUM(ss.ss_quantity)::numeric AS sum_q,
           COUNT(ss.ss_quantity) AS cnt_q,
           SUM(ss.ss_list_price)::numeric AS sum_lp,
           COUNT(ss.ss_list_price) AS cnt_lp,
           SUM(ss.ss_coupon_amt)::numeric AS sum_ca,
           COUNT(ss.ss_coupon_amt) AS cnt_ca,
           SUM(ss.ss_sales_price)::numeric AS sum_sp,
           COUNT(ss.ss_sales_price) AS cnt_sp
    FROM filtered_cd cd
    JOIN store_sales ss ON ss.ss_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
    JOIN filtered_dates dt ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = dt.d_date_sk
    JOIN filtered_promos pr ON ss.ss_promo_sk = pr.p_promo_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_item_sk IN (SELECT i_item_sk FROM top_item_keys)
    GROUP BY ss.ss_item_sk
)
SELECT i.i_item_id,
       SUM(f.sum_q) / NULLIF(SUM(f.cnt_q), 0) AS agg1,
       SUM(f.sum_lp) / NULLIF(SUM(f.cnt_lp), 0) AS agg2,
       SUM(f.sum_ca) / NULLIF(SUM(f.cnt_ca), 0) AS agg3,
       SUM(f.sum_sp) / NULLIF(SUM(f.cnt_sp), 0) AS agg4
FROM fact_agg f
JOIN item i ON f.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
GROUP BY i.i_item_id
ORDER BY i.i_item_id
LIMIT 100

reasoning_trace:
1. FILTERED-DIMENSION DRIVING SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: customer_demographics.cd_demo_sk with cd_gender='F', cd_marital_status='W', cd_education_status='College' and store_sales.ss_cdemo_sk — TRANSFORMATION: Materialize the small set of matching cd_demo_sk values and use it as the outer probe with an index on store_sales(ss_cdemo_sk, ss_sold_date_sk), so only fact rows with qualifying demographics are fetched instead of scanning all 57.6M store_sales rows.

2. DATE-DIM SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: store_sales.ss_sold_date_sk ↔ date_dim.d_date_sk with d_year=2001 — TRANSFORMATION: Apply the 2001 date restriction as a semi-join/bitmap over the 365 d_date_sk values, reducing the fact input to one year before any aggregation or additional joins.

3. PROMOTION FILTER SEMI-JOIN — TARGET: promotion.p_promo_sk with (p_channel_email='N' OR p_channel_event='N') and store_sales.ss_promo_sk — TRANSFORMATION: Precompute the allowed p_promo_sk set and semi-join store_sales on ss_promo_sk, avoiding a full promotion join and removing null/non-qualifying promo rows early.

4. LIMIT-PUSHED ITEM-ID SELECTION — TARGET: item.i_item_id with ORDER BY i_item_id LIMIT 100 — TRANSFORMATION: First compute the first 100 distinct i_item_id values that have qualifying rows via an EXISTS probe against the filtered fact, then run the grouping/aggregation only for those item ids; this avoids sorting and aggregating every item.

5. PRE-AGGREGATION ON FACT ITEM KEY — TARGET: store_sales.ss_item_sk and the aggregate expressions for ss_quantity, ss_list_price, ss_coupon_amt, ss_sales_price — TRANSFORMATION: Aggregate the filtered fact rows per ss_item_sk into SUM/COUNT (not final AVG), then join item and recombine by i_item_id with weighted sums, so the final group/join input is at most one row per item key.

6. COVERING INDEX FOR FILTERED FACT SCAN — TARGET: store_sales(ss_cdemo_sk, ss_sold_date_sk, ss_promo_sk, ss_item_sk) INCLUDE (ss_quantity, ss_list_price, ss_coupon_amt, ss_sales_price) — TRANSFORMATION: Create/use this covering index so the filtered probes and pre-aggregation can be index-only scans, avoiding heap lookups on the large store_sales table.
